# NEAR Intents X-Ray: the thesis

*Generated by `scripts/build_report.py` from `data/derived/numbers.json`. Do not edit by hand: every figure
below is filled in by the build, and every verdict comes from the rules in `thesis_tests.json`.*

## The claim

NEAR's investment case now rests on NEAR Intents. The usual argument is "volume is growing". Volume is a
number NEAR publishes about itself, so we asked two harder questions of the contract:

1. **Is the demand real and broad?** Does the published volume show up on-chain, from many chains, as the
   kind of flow that persists (dollars moving) and not only as speculation?
2. **Is the structure sound?** Who settles the flow, who submits it, and how much of it does NEAR keep?

## Investment view

The demand is real; the weak points are structural. On-chain flow passes 2 of 3 demand tests: it reconciles with the published volume and most of it is stablecoins, so it behaves like a cross-chain dollar rail (whether any one chain supplies half of it is not settled by two samples). That is the bull case, and it is checkable. The structure fails 2 of 3 tests: five relayer accounts submit 97% of all transactions and NEAR keeps only 4.9 bps of the volume. So the long-term case for the NEAR token is not "Intents volume goes up". It is "NEAR opens up who can submit transactions and raises its take without losing the volume". This repository measures each of those, and can be re-run to see whether they move. And one finding cuts both ways: 78% of the value we can see being settled now moves through Confidential Intents, a ledger outsiders cannot audit. That is real demand for privacy, and it also means the public evidence this thesis rests on is shrinking.

## The finding we did not expect

The account at the centre of the public ledger is not an anonymous whale. NEAR's documentation names
`51e8f94d77b5e90dc9852ca6113771e11e8382ce69473a75e313e41665de7cbe` as the **Confidential Intents Treasury** (https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/market-makers/confidential-example): a transfer into it is the "shield"
step of a confidential swap, and the swap itself then executes against a separate private contract.

About $85M a day is shielded into Confidential Intents ($59M to $116M), in roughly 30,695 transfers a day. Swaps that settle in the open on the public contract come to about $27M a day. So of the value we can see being settled either way, 77.6% (95% CI 71.5% to 83.7%) goes to the confidential side (two samples pooled). In the main sample the share was 59% in the earlier 15 days and 88% in the later 15.

- **For the thesis:** privacy is a product most cross-chain venues do not have, and the flow has moved to it.
  Shielded value alone is 0.55× (95% CI 0.42× to 0.68×) of the published daily volume.
- **Against it:** from the public chain we can count what enters and leaves the treasury, not who traded what with
  whom. As the confidential share grows, the published volume becomes harder for outsiders to check.
- **Open question:** the treasury backs every shielded balance. Who holds its keys, and under what controls, is not
  visible on-chain.
- **Caveat:** solvers also shield their own liquidity to fill confidential swaps
  (37% of shielded value comes from named accounts), so shielded value is
  an upper bound on confidential swap size, not a measure of it.

### When it happened

Up to 2026-10-30, 21.8% (95% CI 19.7% to 23.8%) of transactions carried a swap settled in the open. From 2026-10-31 it is 3.5% (95% CI 2.8% to 4.3%). Open swaps fell from about $38M to $16M a day while shielded value rose from $54M to $113M a day. The share has been under 3% on every one of the last 10 full days (since 2026-11-04), with open swaps averaging $2M a day. Re-drawing the sample 1,000 times puts the break between 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-03 in 95% of draws.

Published volume did not fall with it: $126M a day before, $132M after. Swaps we can see in the open were 30% of the published figure before the break and 12% after. The rest of the published number now has to be taken on trust.

### Who shields

2,770 different accounts shielded funds in the sampled windows. Two solver accounts, solver-priv-liq.near and solver-multichain-asset.near, supply 36% of the shielded value between them; the ten largest shielders together account for 61.2% (95% CI 44.7% to 72.8%). Accounts that each contribute under 1% make up 34%. So use is broad by count, with solver liquidity as the largest single block.

### What the treasury holds

At block 224,532,448 (2026-11-14 15:23 UTC) the treasury held $129M on the public contract, in 174 assets; 33% of it stablecoins. About $113M a day has been shielded since the break, so the pool turns over roughly every 1.1 days. The holdings are readable by anyone; the shielded balances they back are not published, so outsiders cannot confirm that one covers the other.

## What we measured

A stratified random sample of `intents.near`: 720 windows of 40
blocks, one per 6,000-block stratum, covering 2026-10-16 to 2026-11-14
(29 days). Every transaction in every window was downloaded: 22,323 in total.
99.7% of token legs were priced. Each window stands for 150 windows of
the population. Intervals are 95%, from a bootstrap over whole windows.

A second, independent sample of the same period (360 windows, 11,284 transactions,
different seed) was drawn to replicate every test.

## Scorecard

For T1 to T5 the measured value is the pooled estimate of two independent samples (1,080 windows). A verdict needs
two things: the whole pooled 95% interval on one side of the threshold, and both samples' own point estimates on that
side. Otherwise the test is inconclusive. T6 uses the public revenue series and has no interval.

| Test | Claim | Passes if | Measured (95% interval) | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T1 | The published volume is real: value entering the contract on-chain matches it | 0.5× to 2.0× | 0.70× (0.56× to 0.84×) | **supported** (main: supported; replication: inconclusive; pooled: supported) |
| T2 | Demand is multi-chain: no single chain supplies half of the deposits | below 50% | 29.2% (21.6% to 36.8%) | **inconclusive** (main: supported; replication: inconclusive; pooled: supported) |
| T3 | It is a dollar rail: stablecoins are most of the value moved | above 50% | 72.5% (66.4% to 78.5%) | **supported** (main: supported; replication: supported; pooled: supported) |
| T4 | Settlement is NOT concentrated: no single account sends half of the value | below 50% | 44.2% (39.1% to 49.4%) | **inconclusive** (main: supported; replication: inconclusive; pooled: supported) |
| T5 | Access is NOT concentrated: the five busiest signers submit under 90% of transactions | below 90% | 97.6% (97.4% to 97.8%) | **contradicted** (main: contradicted; replication: contradicted; pooled: contradicted) |
| T6 | NEAR captures value: revenue is at least 5 bps of volume (30 days) | above 5.0 bps | 4.9 bps | **contradicted** |

## Evidence for the bull case

- **T1.** Value entering the contract in our sample is 0.79× (95% CI 0.57× to 1.06×) of the volume NEAR publishes for the same 28 days. The headline number is not an artefact of a dashboard: money of that order shows up on-chain. A second check agrees: the sample's transaction count is 0.97× the exact count. The independent replication sample measures 0.66× (95% CI 0.49× to 0.84×); pooling both samples gives 0.70× (0.56× to 0.84×). The verdict holds.
- **T3.** Stablecoins are 72.8% (95% CI 63.1% to 80.4%) of the value moved inside the ledger. This is a dollar-transfer product more than a trading venue. The independent replication sample measures 72.2% (95% CI 63.6% to 80.4%); pooling both samples gives 72.5% (66.4% to 78.5%). The verdict holds.

## Evidence against it

- **T5.** Five accounts submit 97.5% (95% CI 97.2% to 97.7%) of every transaction that touches the contract. End users almost never sign a NEAR transaction themselves (1.6% of transactions are signed by an unnamed user account). The independent replication sample measures 97.8% (95% CI 97.4% to 98.1%); pooling both samples gives 97.6% (97.4% to 97.8%). The verdict holds.
- **T6.** NEAR's captured revenue is 4.9 bps of volume over the last 30 days: $1.8M on $3.8B. Users pay 16.0 bps; NEAR keeps 30.5% of that.

## Not settled by this sample

- **T2.** The largest source chain, NEAR, supplies 30.9% (95% CI 16.1% to 44.9%) of deposits. The top three (NEAR 31%, Tron 29%, Ethereum 21%) are close enough that the leader changes between robustness runs; none comes near half. Demand does not hang on one chain. The independent replication sample measures 50.7% (95% CI 34.7% to 63.2%), led by Ethereum; pooling both samples gives 29.2% (21.6% to 36.8%). The two samples' point estimates fall on opposite sides of the threshold, so the claim is marked inconclusive even though the pooled interval passes.
- **T4.** The largest sender moves 40.6% (95% CI 34.1% to 46.4%) of the value, so the test as written passes: no single account sends half. But read it with this: that account is on one side or the other of 86.7% (95% CI 78.2% to 92.6%) of the value, and it is not an anonymous whale. NEAR's own documentation names it as the Confidential Intents Treasury: a transfer into it is the "shield" step that moves funds onto the confidential ledger, and a transfer out of it is the unshield. Every one of the 5,964 sampled transfers into it carries a long opaque memo (120 to 184 characters), and none of the 14,566 other transfers does. That matches the documentation, which says the shield memo carries the encrypted recipient. We stored only the memo's length; the one we re-fetched in full is base64 data. The independent replication sample measures 52.9% (95% CI 43.6% to 62.6%); pooling both samples gives 44.2% (39.1% to 49.4%). The two samples' point estimates fall on opposite sides of the threshold, so the claim is marked inconclusive even though the pooled interval passes.

## The numbers behind the view

- Estimated flow: deposits $109.4M a day ($76.8M to $149.4M),
  withdrawals $86.7M a day, internal transfers $184.2M a day,
  114,889 transactions a day. Published volume for the compared days: $128.9M a day.
- Sampling check: the sample's transaction count is 0.97× the exact count for the same days.
- Largest sender `51e8f94d77b5e90dc9852ca6113771e11e8382ce69473a75e313e41665de7cbe`: 40.6% (95% CI 34.1% to 46.4%) of value sent, present in 92% of windows,
  4,608 counterparties in the sample.
- Confidential Intents Treasury `51e8f94d77b5e90dc9852ca6113771e11e8382ce69473a75e313e41665de7cbe`: on one side or the other of 86.7% (95% CI 78.2% to 92.6%) of value moved by transfers (main sample).
- Second settlement path: token_diff swaps are 22% of trade events, about $26.7M a day,
  across 1,725 accounts; the largest, `solver-priv-liq.near`, has 29.1% (95% CI 14.0% to 38.0%).
- Largest receiver `51e8f94d77b5e90dc9852ca6113771e11e8382ce69473a75e313e41665de7cbe`: 46.1% (95% CI 41.1% to 50.6%) of value received.
- 34 standing accounts (seen in at least 5% of windows) out of 7,402 accounts;
  87.9% (95% CI 80.1% to 93.9%) of value has a standing account on at least one side.
- Source chains: NEAR 30.9%, Tron 29.5%, Ethereum 20.6%, Zcash 7.3%, Solana 4.6%.
- Destination chains: Tron 27.8%, Ethereum 24.1%, NEAR 17.0%, BNB Chain 10.0%, Solana 7.7%.
- Assets: USDT 48.1%, USDC 22.9%, BTC 6.1%, ZEC 4.8%, WNEAR 4.6%; stablecoins 72.8% (95% CI 63.1% to 80.4%).
- Signers: `intents.near` 63.3%, `escrow.ai.near` 14.2%, `bridge-mng.near` 12.6%, `omni-relayer.bridge.near` 6.8%; top five 97.5% (95% CI 97.2% to 97.7%).
- Value capture, last 30 days (2026-10-14 to 2026-11-12, DefiLlama): volume $3.8B, fees paid by users
  $6.0M (16.0 bps), revenue captured by NEAR $1.8M (4.9 bps),
  annualised $22.4M.

## The track's starting hypothesis, tested

The official prompt proposes that Intents volume is a better indicator of real usage than token price.
Using exact daily transaction counts for `intents.near` (2026-10-05 to 2026-11-12, 39 days):

| Daily change in intents.near transactions vs | same day | previous day | levels |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Intents volume (published) | +0.40 | -0.05 | +0.29 |
| NEAR price | +0.12 | -0.04 | -0.61 |

These are correlations over a short window, not proof of a lead. "Previous day" asks whether yesterday's
change in volume or price goes with today's change in transactions.

29 of 39 re-checks give the same verdict as the main sample. No verdict flips to the opposite side. Differences: T1 is inconclusive in “Replication sample” (supported in the main sample); T2 is inconclusive in “Replication sample” (supported in the main sample); T4 is inconclusive in “Replication sample” (supported in the main sample); T1 is inconclusive in “Third sample” (supported in the main sample); T2 is inconclusive in “Third sample” (supported in the main sample); T4 is inconclusive in “Third sample” (supported in the main sample); T1 is inconclusive in “Older half only” (supported in the main sample); T3 is inconclusive in “Older half only” (supported in the main sample); T2 is inconclusive in “Recent half only” (supported in the main sample); T4 is inconclusive in “Recent half only” (supported in the main sample). T5 gives the same verdict in every run, and the treasury's share is between 86% and 92% in every run. T2 and T4 depend on a few very large deposits and transfers, so the headline marks them inconclusive. "Whales removed" is not a fair test of T1, because large deposits are about half of the value by construction.

## Context: peers, price and timing

- **Peers.** DefiLlama has both volume and revenue for 4 of these 9 venues. Among them NEAR Intents keeps 4.7 bps, ranking 2 of 4. The venues of comparable size keep less: Unit 2.4 bps and Maya Protocol 0.9 bps. By revenue in dollars it is first of the 9. This cuts against our own T6 objection: the 5 bps bar was ours, and the comparable venues we can measure do not clear it either.
- **Price.** NEAR's market value is $4.09B, which is 182× annualised Intents revenue ($22.4M). At a 30× multiple, revenue alone would have to be 6.1× today's. This ignores everything else the token is valued for.
- **Take around the break.** NEAR's take was 4.9 bps of published volume before the break and 4.0 bps after; what users paid went from 15.5 bps to 15.1 bps. The timing matches; we have no evidence of cause.
- **Timing.** Transactions lean a little towards 09:00–17:00 UTC and away from weekends. Software alone would not slow down at weekends, so this hints at people behind the five relayers. It is a weak hint: each hour rests on about 30 windows, single busy windows move the line, and the end users never appear as the signer here.

## Predictions (registered 2026-11-14, graded 2026-12-14)

Each prediction is checked against every daily tracker row dated AFTER the registration day (data/history/tracker.jsonl). A prediction is met on a day when that row's point estimate satisfies the rule. On the horizon date it is graded 'held' if it was met on at least 80% of tracked days, otherwise 'failed'. The registration-day row is shown as the baseline and is not scored, because it was visible when these were written.

| | Prediction | Met when | Baseline | Days met | Status | If we are wrong |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | Access stays closed: the five busiest signers keep submitting at least 90% of transactions | ≥ 90.0% | 98.4% | 9 of 9 days | on track | Relayer access is opening up. The main structural objection in this thesis weakens. |
| P2 | The move to confidential settlement is permanent: at least 90% of visibly settled value is shielded | ≥ 90.0% | 99.7% | 7 of 9 days | off track | The collapse of public swaps was temporary, and the audit gap is smaller than we say. |
| P3 | NEAR's take stays under 5 bps of published volume, measured over the trailing 30 days | < 5.0 bps | 4.9 bps | 9 of 9 days | on track | Value capture is improving. The second structural objection weakens. |
| P4 | It remains a dollar rail: stablecoins stay above half of the value moved | > 50.0% | 58.4% | 8 of 9 days | on track | The flow is turning speculative, and the demand case needs rewriting. |
| P5 | Demand persists: published volume stays at or above $100M a day | ≥ $100M | $176M | 9 of 9 days | on track | The volume was a one-month spike, and the bull case falls. |

## What would change our mind

- **T1 fails on a re-sample.** If deposits fall wholly outside 0.5× to 2× of published volume, the demand is not verifiable and the thesis falls.
- **The top five signers fall below 90% of transactions.** The access dependency is easing.
- **NEAR publishes verifiable aggregates for the confidential ledger** (volume, solver count, treasury controls). The audit gap closes and the confidential share becomes a plain positive.
- **Revenue holds above 5 bps of volume for three months without volume falling.** The value-capture objection is answered.
- **One chain rises above half of deposits.** The product has become a single-corridor bridge and should be valued as one.

## What this cannot tell you

- Thresholds were fixed after a 6-window pilot and before the full sample was drawn, and were not changed afterwards.
- The rule for combining the two samples was written after both were drawn. Under a stricter rule (each sample must
  pass alone) T1 would also be inconclusive: the replication interval starts at 0.49×.
- T1 compares deposits with published swap volume: the same order of magnitude is the test, not equality.
- It is a sample. Value shares are noisy because a few very large transfers carry much of the value (median transfer
  $1.53, largest $1.1M; transfers of $100K or more are 52.9% (95% CI 37.2% to 65.8%) of value).
- Amounts are valued at each day's USD price (99.0% of legs); intraday moves are not captured.
- One account is identified from NEAR's public documentation (the Confidential Intents Treasury). All others are described by
  behaviour; we do not claim to know who operates them, and one operator may run several.
- The confidential side is seen from outside only: what happens on the private contract is taken from NEAR's documentation, not observed.
- Concentration in the treasury is by design. It is a custody and governance dependency, not evidence of wrongdoing.
- User counts cannot be read from this contract: 97% of accounts appear in one window only.
- The published volume and revenue series are NEAR's own Dune tables as relayed by DefiLlama. T1 checks the volume; we did not
  independently re-derive revenue.
- The BigQuery cross-checks in `sql/` were not executed, and the Intents Explorer API (partner JWT) was not used.
- Research, not investment advice.
